title: RememberDryRunResponse
description: GAP-SG-216: response emitted by `sqlite-graphrag remember --dry-run`. A DIFFERENT shape from remember.schema.json, which requires memory_id, version and thirteen other members a run that wrote nothing cannot supply — so the dry run satisfied no published schema at all until v1.2.8. It now reports what the validation actually learned: the parsed graph sizes and every non-canonical entity_type, the same warnings the real path emits for the same input.

dry_run.description: Discriminator. Always true; the real run emits remember.schema.json instead and never carries this member.

name.description: Normalized kebab-case name the write would use, not necessarily the one typed.

planned_action.description: would_update only when the memory exists AND --force-merge was given.

entities_parsed.description: Entities the graph payload yielded, after the per-memory limit was applied.

relationships_parsed.description: Relationships the graph payload yielded, after the per-memory limit was applied.

warnings.description: Declared entity_type labels outside the thirteen recommended kinds, phrased as `entity_type 'X' on entity 'Y' is outside the canonical set`. Since v1.2.8 the vocabulary is OPEN, so this is an advisory and the label would be stored as written; under `--strict-entity-types` the same list is what refuses the write with exit 1 instead. Empty rather than absent when every label is canonical, so a consumer never has to distinguish the two.

truncated.description: GAP-SG-142: raised by the agent-native surface whenever it removed data from this envelope.

count.description: GAP-SG-142: emitted under --count-only, which replaces the payload.

examples.name: alice-onboarding-checklist
